# `covers` is how many cases that one skip LINE stands for, and it is
# the field that matters: on a stock runner `tools/test-hazlint.sh` prints eight

# arrives at 40. All three come out of `R2a/b/d-2`, and the one worth reading is
# hazlint's: the tool had been scanning a MIPS16 region four bytes at a time, so
# the cases added are a REFUSAL and its two mutations rather than more coverage of
# what it already did. test-isa-probe's A1 is the same shape one level up -- it
# asserts that a missing toolchain produces no table at all.
# 2026-08-27: test-hazlint 56 -> 96 and test-rlxprobe 195 -> 202, both from the
# COP3 correction in hazlint 1.2. Note what did NOT move: no violation count on
# any artefact in this tree changed, on either tool, before or after. The whole
# of the delta is controls and mutations -- which is the only way a fix that
# moves no number can be shown to have been a fix at all.
# 2026-08-26: spec-check went 10 -> 11 when it gained C8 and a ninth mutation.
# Caught by running ci-census against a fresh spec-check.out BEFORE the push --
# the second time a number in this repository would have been contradicted by
# the very next build (the first was ci.yml's own header, 2026-08-25).
# 2026-08-27 (second session): binsim arrives with two rows. `binsim` is the
# tool's own --self-test, twenty-three controls, none of which needs a vendor binary
# -- deliberately, because hazlint is *bench-only* for exactly the opposite
# reason and that means CI runs zero hazlint cases. `test-binsim` is 71 on the
# bench and 63 on a runner; the eight that stand down are the ones that read the
# six vendor trees. That eight was SEVEN when this row was first written, and
# the arithmetic here is what said so -- 48 + 7 = 55 against a bench total of 56,
# one short, because the section it stands for had eight cases and not seven.
# The suite was 56 then and is 65 now: `--fingerprint` turned out to have no case
# at all (seven added), and E0 -- the corpus's one-ISA membership rule -- got two
# more when a 2025 MediaTek image raised the question of a seventh tree; then 65 ->
# 71 when an adversarial review found three surviving mutants and a manifest no
# runner could reach.
# 2026-08-27 (third session), R2a/b/d-1: binsim 23 -> 24 and test-binsim 71 -> 96.
# The gate's step replaced the plan's refuted `@floor`, and the count is what
# that cost. Two things drive it.
# One: the real corpus stopped taking the REFUTED branch, and that branch had
# no fixture anywhere else -- a verdict that has stopped firing is not one that
# has been satisfied, it is one nobody is watching. So the verdict became a
# function (`floor_verdict`), `D5` drives it in both directions AND varies its
# second argument, `M11` inverts it, `M12` is the mutant that ignores CROSS
# entirely (an adversarial reviewer BUILT that one and it survived D5's first
# version), and `X` builds a second synthetic corpus that lands on the refuted
# side.
# Two: the step's first answer was wrong and the review caught it. `@floor` had
# been moved to `busybox unit-2018/v3.4.0` = 0.1646, which clears CROSS 0.1581
# -- but containment divides by the SMALLER feature set, and busybox's is 1.46x
# boa's, so the two numbers were read at different denominators. At a matched
# denominator the ordering reverses. The floor is now the CROSS cell itself in
# the new five-field cross-program form, `E7` asserts it is the top of a
# three-program population at ONE denominator, and `E8` measures what a
# compilation-model change alone costs (`@model`, pppd 2.4.4 in two trees).
# The corpus gained three `baseline` rows for that: 18 -> 21.
# The R section went 8 -> 22, and the shape of the new fourteen is the point:
# two read the PREMISE of the floor choice rather than its consequence (one
# BusyBox version and one boa version across all six trees), two pin that BASE
# and FLOOR share a denominator, three pin the population E7 takes a maximum
# over, two pin E8's reading, and two sweep the named cell's rank over k in
# both directions -- it is overtaken at k=1, which is what makes the other five
# rows mean something.

column1: spec-check
column5: 11 -> 23 on 2026-08-30 (tenth session). C8 stopped being about SPEC.md: it now runs over every tracked `.md` outside `upstream/` -- 71 files, 620 tables, ~3,600 rows, ~43,000 code spans -- because how this repository's prose renders is not a property of one file. 量 the first time it ran that way: EIGHT ragged rows against a census that had said six, because that census had looked at three files. Three more shapes came with it, each found by turning the previous one on: C8b a row split over more than one PHYSICAL line (two instances, and one of them blinded every checker here to the rest of its table), C8c a `|`-line belonging to NO table (NINE rows of docs/FINDINGS.md -- the page a reader is pointed at, including the three newest findings -- plus one of bench/README.md; C8 cannot see this by construction, since C8 walks tables and a stranded row is in none), and C9 a code span whose whole content is whitespace (FOUR instances, one of which made a READING wrong rather than a rendering: docs/loader-command-semantics.md annotated BOTH exits of readline's three-way branch with the same empty character; the fourth is the carried-forward row that DESCRIBES the defect, and only running the finished checker over `git archive HEAD` found it -- the count assembled one file at a time said three). Whole reading over the tree at HEAD: C8 8, C8b 2, C8c 10, C9 4 -- 24 defects in six files. The twelve new case lines are ten fixture controls plus their summary and the sweep's own report. T1 is the POSITIVE one and is why the rest mean anything -- a checker that fires on everything passes every mutation; T5 is a control on that control (with the fence mask off, the clean fixture must go red); T7 refuses on a population that is empty, has no SPEC.md, or descends into upstream/. The fixture is built in the process, not committed, so all twelve run anywhere git does 🔄 23 -> 30 on 2026-08-30 (twelfth session, after the seating). `C10` is new: a paragraph whose backtick RUNS cannot pair, so a code span is left open and swallows the prose after it. It exists because `C9` pairs runs across the WHOLE FILE, which makes an unmatched run invisible until later text happens to supply a partner -- order dependent, and 量 that is what hid three of these. One had been committed for a day with every other check passing over it: `notes/kernel-build.md` rendered a whole sentence as code while `0x2B0000`, the number the sentence is about, rendered as prose; `RUNSHEET.md` closed a span with a run of TWO, which leaves the backtick COUNT even so a parity test misses it. Seven new case lines: T11 (an opening run that never closes), T14 (the doubled closer -- run LENGTH against backtick COUNT, the shape a parity implementation passes T11 and misses), T15 (two paragraphs with one unclosed run each, which pins the PARAGRAPH boundary: an implementation pairing file-wide reports none), T12 (the negative -- a paragraph whose runs pair is clean), T13 (a control on the EXEMPTION: the one frozen prediction block that cannot be repaired must still fire without its entry, so a repaired file forces the entry out instead of hiding a later defect), T16 (a file with no trailing newline -- every other control appends text ending in one, so the trailing yield was never exercised) and T17 (the finding names the paragraph's first line, COMPUTED from the fixture rather than hardcoded). 🔴 T14, T16 and T17 exist because `tools/test-spec-check-mutants.py` ran twelve mutants against the first version and THREE survived. All seven run on the built-in fixture, so this adds 7 to the run total and 0 to `not-run-total` 🔄 30 -> 40 on 2026-08-31 (eighteenth session): `C11`, a reference to a line of a payload source must carry a TOKEN from that line and the token must still be within three lines of the number. It exists because editing `probe3.c` on 2026-08-31 invalidated fourteen `probe3.c:NNN` references at once and the OWNER AUDIT, not a checker, is what found them -- the line still exists, so "does this line exist" passes, and nothing compared the line to what the citing sentence says is there. Ten case lines: T17 (a correct reference is clean), T18 (a bare line number), T19/T19b (a token elsewhere in the file / nowhere), T20a+T20b (one edge each of the +-3 tolerance -- a single case at a boundary passes whether the comparison is < or <=), T20c (a token holding a pipe, caught before it breaks the row it sits in), T23 (a reference to a file that is not a payload source is out of scope), and two POPULATION controls on the real tree: T21 the live population is not empty, T22 the record-file exemption is load-bearing. 🔴 It went red on its first run over this repository and the finding was the format's OWN exemplar, written the day before: `res_put(R_W_ASSOC + 1u)` is not a substring of the line it cites. It went red a second time the same day, on the sixteen references Group F's edit to `probe3.c` moved -- which is the whole workflow. The fixture SOURCE is injected rather than read from `tools/rlxprobe/`, so these cases do not fire on the next payload edit; all ten run anywhere git does and add 0 to `not-run-total`

column1: test-console-capture
column5: 29 -> 40 on 2026-08-30 with the terminator guard and the two metadata fields (R3-9). Eleven cases, of which **seven are controls** under this file's own definition (a case whose id begins `N` — the tool must refuse, or a mutant must break a case above); the suite's header count moves 17 → 24 by exactly those seven: N18/N20 (the refusal, and that an explicit `--seconds 0 --idle 0` is the same request in longhand), N19 (it fires before the port is opened -- the ordering _check_send exists for), N21 (the sandwich: a 127-char --send with no terminator must hit the TERMINATOR refusal, which proves the guard sits after the length check and before the port, from one command), N22 (both metadata fields move with their arguments, so they are recorded rather than constant), N23 and N24 (the two mutations -- guard dead, fields hardcoded). P13 is not a duplicate of P12: a guard written on --seconds alone passes P12 and refuses every --idle capture, including RUNSHEET D1, whose measured quantity IS a silence. 🔴 P4 CHANGED rather than being added to: it now passes --seconds 1, because its assertion is that a 127-character line REACHES the port, and 量 2026-08-30 it is the only one of this file's four terminator-less invocations that the guard reaches -- N4, N7 and N8 are refused inside _check_send first. All eleven run on a stock runner (a pty, no device), so this row adds 11 to the run total and 0 to `not-run-total`. 🔄 That total is **455**, not the 452 this sentence said when it was written: `flashwin` arrived in the same session and moved it by 3. A row that names the total it does not change still has to name it correctly 🔄 40 -> 46 the same day, and the reason is the only kind that counts: tools/test-console-capture-mutants.py ran 25 mutants of the terminator guard against those forty cases and TEN survived. They fell into four classes and not one of the forty could see a class rather than an instance. N25/N26 close WAIVER (an early `return` on any flag the cases leave at default -- `if args.esc > 0: return` passed all forty, and `--esc 25` is A-catch's own shape; 量 on a pty that mutant gives rc=124 with the .meta.json lost). N27 closes CONTRACT, both halves in one case: no case asserted an exit code, so `SystemExit(0)` was green and a card written `cmd || abort` would read a refusal as success; and none looked at stdout, so a refusal printed there was green too. N28 closes MESSAGE (one substring passed a refusal naming `--timeout`, a flag that does not exist). N29/N30 close POSITION, which N21 only appeared to cover: N21 sends 127 characters, a line _check_send ACCEPTS, so it passes whether or not the guard sits above it -- N29 sends 128 and requires the LENGTH refusal, and N30 pre-creates the output files and requires the TERMINATOR refusal ahead of the overwrite one. All six drive --port /dev/null and add 0 to not-run-total

column1: test-console-capture-mutants
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (tenth session), and it exists because test-console-capture reported 40/40 while TEN mutations of the guard it had just gained were alive. "Nine survived" had been a sentence in LOG.md that nothing re-ran; this is what makes it a number that can go red. Same shape as test-rbcheck.py. Each row edits console-capture.py at anchors that must occur EXACTLY ONCE -- a moved anchor is reported as a SURVIVOR, never skipped -- and requires the WHOLE of test-console-capture.sh to go red against the result; a proxy for the suite would be a different claim. The 25 are 8 WAIVER, 5 CONDITION, 3 POSITION (a move is two edits, so writing it as one would be a delete), 3 CONTRACT/MESSAGE, 4 METADATA, and 2 on _check_send itself -- those last two are there because if either survives, the guard's cases are covering for _check_send's and P1 is being killed by luck. It refuses outright if the unmutated suite is not green, since every mutation would then "kill" on a suite that was already red. Mutants run 8 at a time because the cases are sleep-bound (ptys and played gaps), not CPU-bound: 量 on this host, 336 s wall for 24 against an 84 s baseline. Needs a pty and python3-serial and nothing else -- no device, no $FWRE_WORK -- so all 25 run here and add 0 to not-run-total

column1: test-spec-check-mutants
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (twelfth session) and it exists for the reason `test-console-capture-mutants` proved two days earlier: a green control suite is a claim about the suite. `spec-check` gained `C10` and reported all fifteen table controls green; twelve mutants of `C10` and its two helpers were run against those controls and **three survived** -- the final paragraph never being yielded (invisible because every control appended text ending in a newline), fenced blocks scanned as prose (invisible because the fixture's fences all paired), and the reported line number off by one (nothing asserted it). T16, T17 and a new fixture fence closed all three; 12/12 now. Each row edits `tools/spec-check.py` at anchors that must occur EXACTLY ONCE -- a moved anchor is reported as a SURVIVOR, never skipped -- and requires the WHOLE `--self-test` (nine SPEC.md controls plus seventeen table controls) to go red. 🔴 The harness is the awkward part and it is measured rather than assumed: `spec-check.py` computes ROOT from its own path, so a mutant cannot be run from /tmp. Each one gets a temp root of symlinks to every top-level repository entry (including `.git`, so `git ls-files` still answers, which T7 requires) plus a `tools/` of symlinked siblings and the mutant as a real file; 量, a clean copy through that harness exits 0 and a C10-never-fires mutant exits 2, which is what says the harness is wired up at all. Twelve mutant lines plus the summary = 13 cases, all of them synthetic -- no device, no $FWRE_WORK, no pty -- so this 🔴 13 -> 18 the same evening, and the reason is the one that matters: an adversarial pass found that `main()` returns on `--self-test` **before `check_tables()` is ever called**, and `table_controls` calls the finding functions directly — so **no mutation in `check_tables` or `report_tables` could be killed by this suite's criterion, by construction**. Seven hand-written mutants passed all three CI gates, two of them disabling `C10` repository-wide while every gate stayed green. **Phase 2** plants three real `C10` defects — prose with a shifting pairing, a table row, and a run of three — in a **tracked** file inside the temp root (`bench/README.md`, under `bench/` so a path-prefix exemption is also caught) and runs the **full** tool, requiring the mutant to report **fewer** than the baseline's three. Counting rather than testing for presence is what makes suppressing one of three visible: `P4` and `P5` each suppress exactly one. Phase 2 carries its own positive control — the unmutated tool must report all three, or every row would 'kill' a run that never saw the defect. `P1`/`P2` are the two that were invisible before. ⚠️ Two rows had to be remodelled on the way: `P2`'s anchor occurred twice and `P5`'s mutation stepped past the first backtick of a three-run so the run became a two-run and the defect still fired — the label said "not counted" and the edit said "counted shorter". Both were reported as SURVIVOR rather than skipped, which is the design. adds 18 to the run total and 0 to `not-run-total`

column1: leakscan
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (thirteenth session) and is rebuilt the day after (fourteenth). It exists because the whole of this repository's leak checking was ONE CI step over `bench/**/*.log` -- 240 files out of the 898 `git ls-files` returns (899 lines, one of them the submodule gitlink). 量: the 658 tracked files it never reads, plus `upstream/`'s 302 that `git ls-files` cannot see at all -- 960 unread -- and it imports audit-bench-log.py's PATTERNS/ALLOW rather than copying them (TC-j) and NEVER PRINTS WHAT MATCHED. 🔄 6 -> 16 on 2026-08-30 (fourteenth session), and the ten new controls exist because the FIRST day's finding was wrong in every clause: it reported one MAC on `FC:19:28`, called that TOTOLINK's OUI, and recorded the attribution as undetermined because FW-17's SSID correlation could not be run. 量: `FC:19:28` is Actions Microelectronics (IEEE MA-L, 2020-08-25); the value equals the `enx<12hex>` interface name in nine tracked files, is the source of the echo REPLIES in both committed host captures and never of the requests, and occurs 0 times in this unit's own 4 MiB dump -- it is the WORKSTATION's USB GbE adapter and never was the device's. The correlation that could not be run was never the only one available: the dump is the arbiter and it was on the disk the whole time. `--attribute` replaces the prefix guess with that lookup and L7-L14 are its controls, every one on a synthetic 4 MiB-shaped fixture so they run on a runner. L9 is the one the never-print property actually needed -- a throwaway probe written the same day printed a 3-byte OUI into a transcript because its masking covered the file lines it echoed and not the lookup strings it built, and L9 asserts a rendered attribution contains the value in NONE of seven encodings and not the OUI either. L13 pins the ORDER: a measurement (these bytes are in this unit's flash) beats every inference above it (locally administered; a scanner's own literal). L15 reads THIS TABLE and asserts the label below is the label the tool prints -- the fix test-kbuild-cflags needed after CI run 33310864156, because a machine with $FWRE_WORK never prints the skip and so never compares it. 🔴 Only `--self-test` is in CI. The verdict run needs the real dump, and the allowlist it would need is deliberately NOT taken: the device is end of life and the owner's decision on the one UNIT finding is recorded in SPEC.md §18 as a decision rather than as an oversight. 🔄 16 -> 17 the same evening: L17 drives the real path text -> abl.scan -> scan_population -> mac_bytes, because every other control hands `classify` a byte string directly and a decoder that dropped one of the four MAC encodings would make every hit in that form NOVALUE -- classified, counted, and silently never looked up. 16 of the 17 run anywhere git does: 16 to the run total, 1 to not-run-total

column1: test-leakscan-mutants
column5: arrives 2026-08-30 (fourteenth session). It exists because `leakscan.py`'s `main()` RETURNS on `--self-test` before the reporting loop runs, so no control in that suite can reach `populations()`'s use site, the IDENTITY filter in the report, or the per-population totals -- which is exactly where the mutant PROGRESS.md had named lives ("the population filter widened so upstream/ is dropped, which would turn 52 findings into a silent 0"). Same structural hole, and same answer, as test-spec-check-mutants.py. THREE phases: phase 1 mutates the classifier and requires `--self-test` to go red; phase 2 runs the WHOLE tool over a planted synthetic corpus of eight known hits and requires the report's SIGNATURE to change -- per-population triples, per-file line counts and the two summary numbers, because a count of planted lines alone left three mutants alive; phase 3 runs `--attribute` over a corpus planted with a value read OUT OF THE DUMP AT RUNTIME plus a DECOY carrying the same three-byte OUI and a different tail, and requires the tool's stdout to contain the value in none of four encodings. 🔴 The decoy is the original defect in one line: a classifier that matches on the vendor prefix -- which is what audit-bench-log.py's `MAC, bare 12 hex` pattern does -- calls it the device's, and one that requires the whole address does not. 量 2026-08-30: the FIRST run had EIGHT survivors. Three were defects in the mutants themselves (two written against a function the value is not even in scope of; one whose anchor occurred twice and was correctly reported NOT APPLIED rather than skipped). It exists because notes/kernel-build.md 17.7a reasoned its way from /dev/mtdblock0 to /dev/mtdblock1 in a COMMENT, and an argument in a comment is not a check. The fixture is an ELF32 carrying a `.init.ramfs` newc archive, and BOTH writers are independent of anything `build` uses -- a fixture emitted by the code under test would agree with it however wrong both were. column1: rbcheck
column5: arrives 2026-08-29 (R1h-3's seating), and it is the CONTROLS rather than a run against a real block. 🔄 **23 since 2026-08-31, and this description said *Ten* while the count column said sixteen — a drift the owner audit caught while the row was being edited for another reason.** SEVEN MUST FAIL: C2 (probe2 read at RB_POISON_W instead of RB_WORDS -- the off-by-the-margin that made this check FAIL on its first real use), C3 (one flipped bit in w0), C4 (a missing reply line REFUSES rather than summing fewer words -- a --seconds truncation looks exactly like a payload defect), C5 (a margin word that is not poison), C6 (probe2's block when probe3's magic is demanded), C7 (one address read twice with different values). C9 is the row that fails if the seal's re-stamp correction ever becomes a no-op, and C10 pins that the progress ladder is selected BY THE BLOCK: probe2 seals at 0x90, which is probe3's P_CACHEOP, so one hardcoded ladder reads a complete probe2 run as having stopped nine stages early -- which is exactly what this tool did on its first run. Every fixture is bench/2026-08-25b/H2g.log and H2a.log, both committed, so all ten run on a stock runner: it adds 23 to the run total and 0 to this one, and that zero is written down because a session that adds a suite and does not move this number looks exactly like a session that forgot to. 🆕 C17..C23 (2026-08-31) cover the RETAINED bitmap region that arrived with probe3's 707-word block, and they run on a block this tool SYNTHESISES rather than on a capture — stated in the code beside them, because there will be no 707-word capture until the next seating and a control on synthetic data shows the check works, not that the payload does. C16 is deliberately left on the 641-word on-device capture: a control rewritten to match new code stops being evidence about the old one. C22 and C23 exist because writing the mutations FIRST found that C17..C21 could not see two of them — every one of those regions holds only FRESH nibbles inside `kept`, so counting STALE as FRESH, and ignoring the truncation limit, both changed no answer. 🔄 23 -> 33 on 2026-08-31 (eighteenth session), all of it Group F -- probe3's memory-mapped SPI window group, `docs/probe3-cells.md` § 6.8. C24 a consistent Group F passes; C25 a fault inside it voids the group (the handler's own time is inside every bracket); C26 `tc_ticks`' never-written sentinel on a leg; C27 a window that returned sixteen identical words -- a floating bus, which is what qemu's Malta board IS and is why that reading has a control; C28 + C28b one edge each of the 10 % repeatability tolerance; C29 a window faster than uncached DRAM; C31 all seven legs poisoned is a REFUSAL (the `g_timer` gate shut) and C32 a MIX of poisoned and written legs is a defect; 🔴 C30 is the population control and it is the one that would have caught a LENGTH test -- presence is decided by `H_LAYOUT_ROWS - H_LAYOUT_RES`, so a 641- or 707-word capture declines Group F instead of reading it out of the row area. Two of § 6.8.3's six refutation conditions are deliberately NOT here: `f.alias` and `f.sfcr` are predictions about the DEVICE and belong to the card and `check-predictions.py`. Synthetic and committed captures only: 0 to `not-run-total` 🔄 33 -> 40 on 2026-08-31 (nineteenth session, seating 8): C33..C39, the retained bitmap's PAIRING pattern -- `docs/probe3-cells.md` § 6.2a (2). `bmp.rerun.fresh` is the SAME number under two-way and under direct-mapped, so the count never separated them and only the positions do: under two-way victims k and k + kept/2 share a set, under direct-mapped no two of the kept victims ever do. C33 pure pairs, C34 contiguous singletons, C35 the MIXED outcome § 6.2a says refutes the model -- it has to be sayable or a tool that can only emit the two clean verdicts looks identical to one that can emit all three. 🔴 C36 is the POPULATION CONTROL and it is the case a tool without it passes while being wrong: an all-FRESH region pairs every k with k+period trivially, so PURE PAIRING off it is a verdict from a region that says nothing. C37 the empty region. C38 pins the period to kept/2 rather than to the number 256 -- a 256-victim point pairs at 128 and a hardcoded 256 answers ALL SINGLETONS to it. 🔴 C39 is the READING, on `bench/2026-08-31c/K2b-rb.log`: 20 FRESH at {15,16, 231..238, 271,272, 487..494}, ten pairs and no singleton. That capture is committed in this same commit, so C39 runs on a stock runner and `not-run-total` moves by ZERO -- written down because a session that adds seven cases and does not move that number looks exactly like a session that forgot to check.

column5: arrives 2026-08-30, and it exists because rbcheck's own --self-test reported 10/10 while four mutations survived -- M4 (the UART-vs-seal comparison), M7 (the progress-vs-sealed comparison), M8 (the unknown-magic fallback) and M9 (the summation extent, which survived because 637 of the 808 summed words in the only fixture are zero). Two of those four delete exactly what the tool advertises. Nine mutations now, all killed; M20 mutates probe3.c rather than rbcheck.py, because the ladder control used to compare two hardcoded copies in one file and could not see source drift at all. Every mutation runs against committed captures in a temporary tree, so it needs no $FWRE_WORK and no device: 9 to the run total, 0 to this one. 🔄 15 since 2026-08-31: M21..M26 mutate the retained-bitmap branch, and each row NAMES the control it must turn red. M25 SURVIVED on its first run — the truncation limit could be deleted with every control still green — which is what C23 was written for. 🔄 15 -> 25 on 2026-08-31 (eighteenth session): six mutations for Group F (M27..M32), two for the `g_timer` gate (M33/M34), and TWO ROWS THAT ARE NOT MUTATIONS. `B0` -- the unmutated tool must pass IN THE TEMP TREE -- is the row `test-replay-capture-mutants` reported 14/14 without, one day earlier; the root baseline cannot see it because ROOT is complete by construction. `A0` -- every anchor must occur EXACTLY ONCE -- caught a live instance the hour it was written: Group F gave `rbcheck.py` a second `if magic == 0x524C5833 and count > 50:` and M26, written for the retained-bitmap branch, had silently begun mutating Group F's guard instead. It still exited non-zero, so it still read as killed. 🔴 And `W0` -- a kill is only valid if it turned the case the row NAMES red -- found two invalid kills on its first run: M24 and M26 both claim `(kills C17)` and C17 stayed GREEN, because both push the tool into the pre-2026-08-31 one-region branch, which reports and never fails. The fix was the control, not the label: C17 now asserts the branch was ENTERED. A positive control that passes when the check does not run is this repository's own failure mode in the place it is least visible. Needs no device and no $FWRE_WORK: 0 to `not-run-total` 🔄 25 -> 31 on 2026-08-31 (nineteenth session): M35..M40 mutate the pairing analysis, six rows, each naming the control it must turn red. 🔴 M36 is the one worth reading -- it removes the all-FRESH population control, and EVERY other pairing case stays green while it is gone, because not one of them is single-valued. That is the shape this suite exists for. M35 hardcodes the period to 256 (C38), M37 counts each pair from both ends (C33), M38 makes the pairing pass count any written nibble so it disagrees with the counting pass (C22), M39 empties the unpaired list so MIXED can never be reported (C35), M40 empties the pairing pass itself (C33). ⚠️ M38's anchor is written DIFFERENTLY from M22's on purpose: `fresh_positions` compares through a local rather than inline, because a second textually identical line would have made M22's anchor ambiguous -- which `A0` would have caught, and which is why `A0` exists. column5: 🔄 13 -> 19 the same day, after an adversarial pass ran 45 mutants against the first self-test and **24 survived** -- three of them printed this unit's MAC (the rendering written to stdout on the refusal path, the withheld digest printed beside the word `withheld`, and the dump never opened at all). The common cause: every case that could leak used ONE argument triple against an ALL-ZERO dump, and R1/R2 called `render_dw()` in process, so nothing between `open the file` and `format the words` had a control over it. Rewritten: every leak-capable case drives the real command line as a subprocess and asserts stdout is EMPTY, R1/R2 go through `--out` + `cmp`, and the synthetic dump is no longer all zeros. 22 of 22 of the surviving mutants are now killed. R1 and R2 render bench/2026-08-24d/G8a-rd0.log and G8a-rd6.log out of $FWRE_WORK/dumps/flash-n150rt-console-2.bin and require them byte for byte; R3 requires the two 2026-08-16 dumps to be identical over all 4,194,304 bytes. A 4 MiB image of this unit's own flash can never be committed, so the three stand down on a runner. The TEN that run anywhere are the ones that make the skip a skip: C1-C5 pin the rendering and its endianness against a mutant, C6/C7/C8 drive the publication guard as a SUBPROCESS in all three directions (no --out refuses, --out inside the repository refuses and writes nothing, --out outside is accepted and prints no digest), and C9/C10 pin the half-open overlap test at both ends with the off-by-one mutant that would let a straddling window through. 量 2026-08-30 with $FWRE_WORK pointed at an empty directory: 16 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 skip line covering 3, which closes against 19. 🔴 This sentence read "10 ok ... closes against 13" until the tenth session -- both halves were the PRE-rewrite numbers, left in the row whose whole job is to carry the number, while the gate column beside them already said 19 🔄 19 -> 24 on 2026-08-30 (fourteenth session): the `normalise` subcommand and its five controls. A `DW` reply carries the typed command and a `%08X:` address column, both holding the RAM DESTINATION, so two reads of the SAME flash window into DIFFERENT RAM addresses do not `cmp` equal -- which is why the bracket's second half had to reuse the first half's destination, and reusing it costs a control: with one destination, "the RAM already held these bytes" is not excluded and an FLR that did nothing looks like one that worked. N2 is the case that matters (the same window rendered at 0x80B50000 normalises identically to the capture taken at 0x80A00000) and N3 is its control (two different windows do not). N5 refuses a file that is not a DW reply, with nothing on stdout. All five read the two committed 777-byte captures and no dump, so they add 5 to the run total and 0 to not-run-total 24 -> 27 the same evening, and the three new controls came from an adversarial pass rather than from thought: eight mutants of `normalise` against N1-N5 and THREE survived -- a garbage data line under a valid echo (N6), a reply with no data lines at all (N7), and a normaliser that SORTED the words, which would make two windows with the same multiset compare equal and which N3 structurally could not see because its two windows differ in content as well as in order (N8). 🔴 The pass itself had to be re-run: the first attempt reported 8 of 8 killed with every one "killed by C7b,C7c", and 量 the UNMUTATED file through that same symlinked temp root was already 22/24 -- C7b/C7c resolve the repository root with realpath, which a symlink farm sends back to the real tree, so every kill was invalid. The baseline-through-the-harness control that test-spec-check-mutants.py has is exactly what it was missing. All three new controls build their fixture in a temp dir and read no dump: 24 of the 27 run anywhere git does 🔄 27 -> 40 on 2026-08-31 (twentieth session), and the thirteen are `scan`: the THIRD containment shape. `render` governs what may be PRINTED and where a rendering may be WRITTEN; `flrbracket run` governs where a BRACKET's read-back may land; both act when a file is produced. Nothing asked whether a file this repository has ALREADY COMMITTED holds forbidden content -- and K-P3 (seating 8) is a 32 KiB `DW` spanning both H601 RAM destinations whose output lands in bench/, safe only because the experiment came out the expected way. S1 the probe set, S2/S2b positive (S2b is the same window TWICE, which is K-P3's shape), S3/S4 the negatives, S5/S5b the hex channel in `DW` and `xxd` shapes, S6/S8 the two refusals, S7 that a HIT prints where and how many and NO byte in any of four renderings and no digest. S9a-c are real material and skip with R1-R3, so the allowed skip goes 3 -> 6. 🔴 量 on its first sweep: rlxfw's own tree is CLEAN over **1,381** files (`--sweep . --exclude upstream`), while the DEFAULT `--sweep .` reads 1,683 and reports 1 HIT, because `upstream/` -- which the first version of the walk excluded -- is NOT clean: BENCH-LOG.md line 2557 is 16 bytes of H601 as a hexdump, in a public repository, and neither leakscan nor audit-bench-log names that line (both look for the text SHAPES an address takes; a hexdump of flash has none). The default that hid it is gone; `--exclude` is how a sweep declines a tree, on the command line where a reader sees it. 🔴 **40 -> 41 the same evening, and CI is why**: run 33410057391 went RED on `UNEXPECTED-SKIP "this unit's flash dump"` while this suite was 40/40 GREEN on the bench. This session edited the allowed-skip COLUMN and left the two string literals in the tool alone, and `ci-census` counts a skip only on an exact match between the two. **The bench cannot see that class**: with `$FWRE_WORK` present the six cases RUN, no skip line is printed, and no label is ever compared -- the same shape as `test-kbuild-cflags` C1 (run 33310864156), `leakscan` Q1 and `replay-capture` R14, which is now THREE precedents this file records for one defect. column1: flrbracket
column5: arrives 2026-08-31 (sixteenth session). It exists because the `FLR` bracket of seating 7 was driven by a script that is NOT in this repository and whose only demonstrated direction was the safe one: 量 2026-08-31, `flr-window.sh` compared the flash source as the card TYPED it (six hex digits) against the loader's echo (zero-padded to eight), rejected a CORRECT echo, sent `N` and got `Abort!` (bench/2026-08-31/CORRECTIONS-block3.md section 9). Nothing had ever shown it would refuse a WRONG echo, which is the only reason it exists. The core is a pure `classify(reply, src, dst, nbytes, sent)` returning PROCEED/ABORT/REFUSE -- three and not two, because *the loader did not ask* must send NOTHING and *the loader asked about something else* must send `N`. THREE strengthenings over the script it replaces, each measured off the corpus rather than reasoned: the LENGTH field is compared (the third typed argument was unchecked, and 100 -> 1000 is the same typo class as the six-versus-eight digits that fired); the fields are parsed as EXACTLY eight hex digits and compared as integers (which kills zero-padding, hex case and the extra-digit boundary in one move); and the echo must occur EXACTLY ONCE after the operator's own typed line is stripped, because the capture's first line is the operator's bytes coming back and a classifier that searches it reads its own input as the loader's confirmation -- the defect class of commit d008372, one tool over. The corpus is nine real FLR echoes, eight replies to Y and one to N, all from seating 7; Q1 asserts the population is 9/8/1 and present, Q2 re-derives every row's three numbers from that capture's own .meta.json `sent` rather than trusting the table. Seven of the 50 are the containment guard driven as a SUBPROCESS, and the line it draws is at CONTENT and not at mention: an FLR echo holds addresses and no flash bytes, which is why bench/2026-08-31/W-flrh.log correctly names 00006000 and is committed, while the two DW captures of an H601 window -- the pre-read included -- are refused inside this repository. G3 is the control on G1/G2 (a guard that refused everything would pass both), G5 pins the guard ABOVE the port, and G6 names the PRE-READ specifically -- the capture the card expected to be garbage and which held this unit's MAC on 2026-08-31. 🔴 G6's first version searched stderr for `pre-read` and could not fail, because the refusal's own explanatory paragraph contains the words `the pre-read included`; the M18 mutant found it. FORBIDDEN is imported from tools/flashwin.py rather than copied. No device, no pty, no $FWRE_WORK, no vendor artefact -- all 50 run anywhere git does, so this row adds 50 to the run total and 0 to not-run-total. 🔴 D2 arrived last and is the only case that compares this instrument against HARDWARE: the plan `run` would issue for the window `X2` actually ran on cycle 6 must equal what seating 7 put on the wire -- four commands, the DW word count and all three terminators, read out of each capture's own .meta.json rather than out of a table in the tool

column1: xcheck
column5: arrives 2026-09-02 with `TOOL-1`, and it is the first row here whose subject is a PAIR of suites rather than one tool. 量 2026-09-01: `looptime` and `boot-timeline` both read a capture's `.timing` and they disagreed by 0.321-0.350 s on six of fifteen cold captures, while `SPEC.md` `CLK-18` cited the one without the line-transition model. `looptime` was fixed; nothing asserts the CLASS, and `ci-census` counts cases per suite and never across suites. Three identities: the two independent `.timing` parsers must return the same rows, the two offset->time lookups the same timestamp at every probed offset, and `lead - artifact` must equal the read gap between the two anchor bytes EXACTLY -- a tolerance is where a 2 ms anchor error hides. 🔴 `C1`/`C2`/`C3` are the controls that make the sweep's zero mean something, and each one documents a REAL divergence the corpus cannot reach: boot-timeline sorts its rows and looptime does not (and looptime's `at_offset` breaks early, which is correct only on sorted input); a malformed line refuses in one and raises `ValueError` in the other; an empty file refuses in one and returns `[]` in the other. `C4` is their negative control -- comments and blank lines are handled the same by both, so the checker is not merely trigger-happy. `M0` runs the identities unmutated (a harness that kills everything and a harness that tests nothing print the same thing) and `M1`/`M2`/`M3` each bias one side so that one identity, and only that one, goes red. Every fixture is built in a TemporaryDirectory: 18 to the run total, 0 to not-run-total

column1: xcheck-sweep
column5: the same tool over the committed corpus, and it prints exactly ONE `ok` line whatever the corpus holds. 🔴 That is deliberate and it is this table's own lesson: `test-boot-timeline`'s `B2` hardcoded *N cold, M warm* and went red on GitHub on three consecutive seatings, and 16 of this repository's 18 red CI runs are a count about its own contents kept in a second place. The sweep therefore asserts PROPERTIES and reports counts, and the only count it enforces is a FLOOR -- at least one artefact must reach each identity, because a sweep that compares nothing prints the same summary as a clean one. 量 on its first run: 390 artefacts, 3 identities, 0 disagreements, and `X3`'s population is 6 -- the same six captures `notes/dev-loop.md` §6.5 found open on a byte the board did not send, arrived at independently. Five of the six have the two anchor bytes in different reads and the residual equals that gap to the picosecond. Reads only files in the repository: 1 to the run total, 0 to not-run-total

column1: looprun
column5: arrives 2026-09-02 with `R4-3`'s `D3`. 🟢 **The assertion it makes is DERIVED from the build rather than typed**, which is the only thing that makes an unattended loop worth running: `rlxfw-kbuild.sh` computes `RLXFW_SRC_ID` as a sha256 over `config/`, `ID0` prints it on the console, and the run requires the board to print the id S2 just computed. Nobody types that value, so a stale image, the vendor's firmware and the loader's own re-staging of flash after a watchdog reset are all red for the same reason -- `N4` and `N7` are those two cases. 🔴 Every one of `N1`..`N7` requires ONE assertion to fail and the other three to hold: a control set where one broken input trips every check cannot say which check is load-bearing, and the first run of this suite proved that was not academic -- `N1` failed because `A2`'s order check treated a missing mark as out-of-order, so `A1` and `A2` were one check wearing two labels. `N7b` came out of the fix: with no marks present at all `A2` passes on nothing, and it now says VACUOUS rather than ok. `R1`/`R2` are two counts about the plan and BOTH were wrong when written (8 and 3 against 7 and 4); they are re-derived from the docstring's stage table. `R3` is the flash ban -- no rendered command may carry `--allow-autoexec` -- and `R4` requires every capture stage to carry a terminator, which `console-capture.py` refuses without. `M0`..`M4` drive the whole runner in `--mode replay`: unmutated it reports 0, a wrong id, a truncated boot and a missing recipe each report 1, and a run with no capture to assert over is REFUSED rather than vacuously green. `R6` arrived when the plan was found rendering `rtkimage.py build --kernel/--out`, two flags that program does not have -- `cardcheck commands` asks whether a CARD's commands are invocable and nothing asked it of the tool that RENDERS them, while `--mode plan` is supposed to be the card's command column. `M5`/`M6` guard `--skip`: skipping S2 removes the only thing that computes the recipe id, so it is REFUSED rather than left to fail A3 for a reason that looks like a stale image. No build, no port, no board, no $FWRE_WORK: 26 to the run total, 0 to not-run-total
